citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The program of veterinary care was not made available at the time of inspection. A written program of veterinary care is
required to ensure adequate veterinary care is provided for the animals. Each dealer and exhibitor shall employ an
attending veterinarian under formal arrangements. In the case of a part-time or consultant veterinarian, the formal
arrangements shall include a written program of veterinary care. This plan must be completed and made available to
APHIS upon request.
Correct by July 9, 2026

No records of disposition were available at the time of the inspection for all covered animals present at the facility.
Appropriate documentation is essential for proper identification and tracking of animals used in regulated activities to
ensure their humane care, use, and disposition.
Every exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records of acquisition and disposition for all regulated animals, including
animals born on the premises, and assure that all records are kept as required.
Correct by July 18, 2026.

The contingency plan was not made available at the time of the inspection. Inadequate contingency planning may fail to
ensure that the animals at the facility are provided with appropriate protection and care in the event of an emergency.
The licensee must develop, document, and follow an appropriate plan to provide for the humane handling, treatment,
transportation, housing, and care of their animals in the event of an emergency or disaster (one which could reasonably
be anticipated and expected to be detrimental to the good health and well-being of the animals in their possession).
Correct by July 9, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
